title: Verifier-Guided Prompting for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered NetOps Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory trial to test whether constrained prompting plus a deterministic generate→verify→repair loop (≤1 repair) increases deterministic-verifier semantic-correctness when translating operator natural-language intents into low-level device configurations. Design: N=150 synthetic intents drawn from a deterministic generator, execution semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial sampled candidate reused across conditions), model = gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, at most one repair call per intent. Results (artifact-grounded): baseline = 149/150 (99.333%); guarded = 150/150 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.0066667 (≈0.67 percentage points); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Provider accounting: completed episodes = 300; model_calls_used = 151; repair-stage invocations = 1. Interpretation: under the preregistered estimand and shared_initial_candidate semantics the guarded pipeline produced a numerically negligible and statistically nonsignificant improvement over an already near-ceiling baseline. We emphasize a methodological lesson: preregistered NetOps trials require brief baseline-calibration pilots to avoid ceiling effects that invalidate preregistered power assumptions. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the referenced execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Natural-language intent interfaces promise to reduce operator cognitive load by allowing administrators to describe desired network changes in free text that are automatically translated into executable device configurations. Prior work documents that single-pass LLM outputs can contain syntactic errors, omitted steps, or semantic violations that, if executed, risk availability or policy violations [1][2][3]. A common mitigation is a generate→verify→repair architecture in which a deterministic verifier checks candidate configurations against formalized invariants and either rejects the candidate or supplies diagnostic feedback used by an automated repair stage [4][5]. Agentic tool-orchestration analyses further motivate conservative gating because unchecked textual claims can be converted into harmful actions in multi-tool workflows [6].

Research question. After an autonomous literature review and preregistration we posed a confirmatory question: does constrained prompting (structured templates with explicit semantic slots) combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback materially increase deterministic-verifier semantic correctness of NL→configuration translation versus an unconstrained baseline under a paired design?

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, artifactized paired confirmatory trial (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) measuring deterministic-verifier pass/fail on a programmatically generated synthetic corpus (N=150 paired intents). (2) Artifact-backed outcomes showing that, under shared_initial_candidate semantics and a one-repair budget, the guarded pipeline raised verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (+0.67 pp), a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). (3) A methodological recommendation that preregistered NetOps trials incorporate short baseline-calibration pilots and explicitly record generation semantics because these choices materially affect estimands and inferential power.
sections.related_work: Prior evaluations of NL→configuration pipelines report modest semantic-correctness rates in heterogeneous benchmarks and highlight sensitivity to prompt design, model competence, and oracle choice [1]. A second body of work integrates deterministic verification into generation workflows and reports correctness gains when verifier signals drive reranking, prompted repair, or fine-tuning, but effect sizes depend strongly on baseline competence, verifier expressiveness, and repair budgets (TerraFormer and related IaC efforts) [2][3]. Third, mature formal verification tools (NetKAT/KATch and related symbolic engines) can provide deterministic oracles for reachability, isolation, and policy checks and are commonly proposed as gating layers for LLM-derived artifacts; however, tool coverage and abstraction mismatches limit their universal applicability without mapping/unit-test effort [5]. Finally, security analyses show that multi-tool LLM agents can transform false textual claims into harmful actions when gating is absent or inadequate, motivating conservative verifier-based architectures and auditable verdicts [4]. Our trial operationalizes a narrowly constrained guarded architecture, explicitly records generation semantics, and targets verifier-level binary correctness as the preregistered endpoint, situating the experiment within these methodological threads.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The study was preregistered (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) with a frozen analysis plan executed before observing model outputs. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated with an exact two-sided McNemar test on deterministic-verifier pass/fail outcomes. Planned confirmatory sample: N=150 distinct synthetic intents generated deterministically and stratified across intent families (reachability/isolation, ACL-like access changes, VLAN/MTU sequence changes, uplink switchover patterns). Inclusion/exclusion rules (rule-based ambiguity detector, parser/ verifier-coverage checks), a deterministic retry policy for provider timeouts (one retry), and a power target (detect +15 percentage points at ≈80% power) were frozen prior to execution.

Mapping between preregistration labels and executed contrast (required clarification). The preregistration conceptually described a three-condition design: A = baseline free-text prompt, B = constrained-template prompt, and C = constrained + verifier-feedback (guarded). The archived run enforced shared_initial_candidate execution semantics: for each intent exactly one initial sampled candidate was produced and that identical candidate was reused across the paired evaluation of A (baseline) and C (guarded). Under these adapter-enforced semantics the confirmatory estimand corresponds to C vs A (guarded vs baseline) interpreted as the marginal effect of applying at most one repair to a fixed initial sampled candidate. Constrained-only (B) was not executed as an independent first-pass condition in this run (no independent B-first-pass samples); consequently no independent B-vs-A or C-vs-B confirmatory contrasts are reported from the archived artifacts. This mapping is enforced and auditable in the execution manifest (stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 150, repair: 1}).

Adapter semantics, call budgets, and tools. Execution semantics = shared_initial_candidate; model = declared "gpt-5-mini" (provider record: openai_responses); model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset). Because no numeric temperature or fixed random seed was enforced, API responses may be nondeterministic across independent sessions; the preregistration anticipated this and specified sampling semantics explicitly. The deterministic verifier used for the binary endpoint was deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) applying the full_intent_constraint_validation rule. The adapter enforced a maximum of one repair call per intent; provider accounting recorded model_calls_used = 151 and repair-stage invocations = 1.

Scoring and analysis. The primary endpoint was the deterministic verifier pass (binary). The archived scorer produced normalized_configuration strings and diagnostic fields used for automated pass/fail scoring. The preregistered primary analysis used an exact two-sided McNemar test on the paired contingency table (n_11, n_10, n_01, n_00) and computed a paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). The preregistered handling of incomplete pairs was complete_pair_primary (exclude incomplete pairs); sensitivity analyses treating failed guarded outputs as failures were specified but not invoked because no failures occurred. No post-preregistration modifications to the confirmatory analysis were made; reported results follow the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor and archived analysis artifacts.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The run completed as planned: completed_episode_count = 300 and complete_pair_count = 150. Provider accounting: model_calls_used = 151; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0; cache_miss_count = 151. Stage-level counts recorded by the adapter: shared_initial_generation = 150 and repair = 1. Contamination checks and mapping unit-tests passed and no confirmatory exclusions occurred.

Primary numerical outcomes. The paired contingency counts (guarded × baseline) were: n_11 = 149 (both-pass), n_10 = 1 (guarded-only-pass), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-pass), n_00 = 0 (both-fail). Per-condition success rates: baseline_success_count = 149/150 = 0.9933333333333333; guarded_success_count = 150/150 = 1.0. Estimated paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00666666666666671 (≈0.67 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729). These values are reported verbatim from archived analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv).

Repair diagnostics and revision iterations. Only one guarded repair invocation occurred (1/150), consistent with the near-ceiling initial success rate. That single repair converted one initially invalid candidate to a valid configuration under the deterministic verifier. Median revision iterations for guarded episodes = 0 (IQR = 0). Representative validator traces for sampled tasks (000001–000006) are archived and show parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_codes, normalized_configuration, and valid flags that corroborate scorer behavior.

Representative example. Task-000001 (generator_seed = 1) intent: "Migrate edge1 to VLAN 30 and MTU 1600. For safety, shut edge1 down before changing either VLAN or MTU, then restore it to admin up. Do not modify any other interface." Shared-initial and both condition responses returned the expected four-command sequence. Validator diagnostics: parsed_command_count = 4; required_command_count = 4; observed_touched_field_count = 3; valid = true. Shared-initial candidate and normalized strings are archived in execution/responses and scoring traces.
sections.discussion:
Ceiling effect and inferential consequence. The preregistered power calculation assumed a substantially lower baseline success rate (target detectable effect = +15 pp). Observed baseline_success_rate = 0.9933333 left almost no headroom for measurable absolute improvement and produced very low discordant-pair information (only one discordant pair: n_10 + n_01 = 1). As preregistered, the primary confirmatory test was applied without post-lock changes, but the observed ceiling effect invalidated the original detectable-effect assumption and therefore limited the trial's capacity to demonstrate the preregistered target effect.

Why baseline was high. Deterministic task generation produced intents with tightly specified required_sequences, constrained allowed_touched_fields, and verifier-matching invariants. When intents are unambiguous and the verifier covers the required invariants, a single sampled candidate from a competent LLM frequently satisfies the verifier; this interaction explains the observed near-ceiling baseline and underlines how generator design (ambiguity, specification completeness, and difficulty calibration) materially affects observed marginal benefits from repair stages.

Sampling semantics and estimand trade-offs. Shared_initial_candidate semantics isolates the marginal effect of repairing a fixed initial sampled candidate. Alternative semantics—independent per-condition sampling or multi-draw ensembles—answer different operational questions (expected pass rate under independent draws or gains from resampling) and typically increase observed discordant counts at the cost of additional model calls and latency. Experimentalists should choose semantics that match deployment constraints and include model-call cost in power planning.

Operational implications beyond binary pass/fail. The deterministic verifier returns normalized configurations, violation_codes, and detailed diagnostics that support auditable records and targeted human triage. Even when verifier-pass differences are numerically small, guarded pipelines can provide operational observability and structured diagnostics that simplify repair policies and human review.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: adapter-enforced call budgets, session isolation, and mapping unit-tests mitigate cross-condition leakage. Construct validity: deterministic verifier pass/fail is a proxy for semantic correctness and depends on mapping code and verifier coverage; any uncovered verifier-coverage gaps would bias correctness measurement. External validity: experiments used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic small topologies (4–32 nodes); results do not generalize to larger heterogeneous networks or other models. Security: adversarial prompt-injection was not assessed in this confirmatory trial and remains a separate concern requiring adversary-driven evaluation. Conclusion validity: the mismatch between preregistered detectable-effect assumptions and observed baseline highlights the importance of baseline calibration to preserve inferential meaning.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory trial comparing baseline free-text prompting to constrained-template prompting plus a single verifier-guided repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On a deterministic synthetic corpus with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline increased verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (≈0.67 pp), a numerically small and statistically nonsignificant difference (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). The principal scientific lesson is methodological: preregistered NetOps trials should include a brief baseline-calibration pilot (e.g., 20–40 tasks) to estimate baseline success and discordant-pair rates before final N selection. Technically, our artifacts bound the marginal benefit of a one-repair guarded pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics; evaluating independent-sampling semantics, larger repair budgets, model diversity, and production-scale topologies remains future work. All execution and analysis artifacts referenced in this paper are archived in the supplied execution bundle and manifest.

limitations: Single-model constraint: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across models or sizes.

Synthetic corpus and scale: tasks were programmatically generated and limited to verifier-capable toy-to-small topologies (4–32 nodes); external validity to production WANs and heterogeneous vendor CLIs is untested.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract limited repair budget to at most one guarded repair call per intent; different generation semantics or multiple-repair budgets may yield different outcomes.

Ceiling effect and preregistration mismatch: baseline correctness (149/150 ≈ 99.33%) far exceeded the preregistered pilot assumption used for power calculations (planned detectable effect = +15 pp), reducing the trial's ability to demonstrate the preregistered target effect.

Verifier coverage and specification translation: the study measures deterministic validator pass/fail on the preregistered invariants but does not claim safety guarantees beyond the deterministic validator's modeled properties.

Security and adversarial robustness: the experiment did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection or adversary-driven intents; separate targeted studies are required to assess claim-to-action vulnerabilities in agentic NetOps workflows.
